add.title: How this card was made
add.text:
**The files.** A card is a folder named by its date; its whole content is one append-only log:

```
public/framework/ai/2026/10/03/
  page.jsonl        the day: lists its cards
  now/
    page.jsonl      this card: one JSON line per change
```

**The calls.** Three tool calls made it, each appending one line:

```js
create_card({ title: "Now", type: "note", summary: "What the AI agents are doing…" })
// → line 1: {"class": "/framework/ai2/card.js", "title": "Now", "type": "note", …}

page_add({ path: "/framework/ai/2026/10/03/now/",
           item: { id: "working", title: "Working on now", text: "- **Console cleanup:** …" } })
// → {"content": {"add": {"id": "working", "title": "…", "text": "…"}}}
```

**Loading it.** The page replays the log line by line: line 1 picks the class, each `content.add` adds an item to the page's `content` List. The list draws one row per item: its title, then its text as markdown.

**Why the rows drag.** Every content list is drawn sortable on purpose (core/Page `render_content_list`): drop a row elsewhere and one `move` line is appended, so the order is saved like any other change. It's not specific to cards; any page with a content list gets it.

add.title: Topics: one call each way
add.text:
Each topic above is a REAL sub-card, one folder deeper (`now/<topic-slug>/`), the same mechanism `your-prompts-refined-live` already used — not a new one.

**Making a topic:** `create_card({ parent: "2026/10/03/now", title, type: "note" })`, then `page_add` for its body (what was said, the answer, links to the agents on it). The parent card lists it automatically — no second line to write.

**Replying into the right place:** `card_reply({ card: "2026/10/03/now/<topic-slug>", text })` talks into that ONE topic, never the top of the Now card. To answer one statement inside a topic (once sentence ids are wired, see below), `card_reply` takes `re: "<statement id>"` and nests the reply under it.

**Still open:** the owner's own statements aren't yet linked in with sentence ids — that depends on @task-mastermind-prompts-live's remaining per-prompt sub-card wiring (its checklist still has this unticked) and a deeper event break routed to @mastermind-servex. Until then a topic's body is written by hand from the Now card's own log, same as every other section here.

Docs: `/framework/servex/agents/` → "Dictate keeps working if Claude cuts off" → `doc/dictate-backend.md`.

Cost ran far past budget ($5 → raised to $8 → actually ~$59) because of how many real bugs the review loop kept finding in a feature whose whole point is "must actually work" — logged in the task file.
